artists.biography:
Jane's Addiction is an American rock band formed in Los Angeles, California in 1985. The band's original line-up featured Perry Farrell (vocals), Dave Navarro (guitar), Eric Avery (bass) and Stephen Perkins (drums). After breaking up in 1991, Jane's Addiction briefly reunited in 1997 and again in 2001, both times with Avery declining to participate. In 2008, the band's "classic" line-up, featuring Avery, reunited and embarked on a world tour. Avery subsequently left the band in early 2010 as the group began work on new material.
Jane's Addiction was one of the first bands to emerge from the early 1990s alternative rock movement to gain mainstream media attention and commercial success in the United States. Their initial farewell tour launched the first Lollapalooza festival, an alternative rock showcase. As a result, Jane's Addiction became icons of what Farrell dubbed the "Alternative Nation."The band was ranked 35th on VH1's "100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock" list.

perplexity.description:
Sterling Spoon is not an original studio album by Jane's Addiction but a comprehensive vinyl box set released by Rhino Records in 2016. The collection celebrates the legacy of the band's early years, focusing on their foundational period with the original lineup: Perry Farrell, Dave Navarro, Eric Avery, and Stephen Perkins. Musically, the set highlights Jane's Addiction's pioneering blend of alternative rock, punk, and art rock, characterized by Farrell's dynamic vocals, Navarro's inventive guitar work, and the rhythm section's powerful, experimental drive. The box set compiles the band's landmark studio albums, Nothing's Shocking (1988) and Ritual de lo Habitual (1990), which are central to their discography and helped define the alternative rock genre in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

Sterling Spoon also features rare tracks, previously unreleased material, and a complete live recording from December 1990 at the Hollywood Palladium, showcasing the band's formidable stage presence and improvisational energy. The release marked a significant moment for fans, offering a curated retrospective of Jane's Addiction's most influential era. While not a new album, the box set was well-received for its comprehensive content and high-quality presentation, serving as both a celebration of the band's impact and a valuable archival release for collectors and longtime listeners.
